result.name: tabs.hold
result.description: Keep tabs an ardia command session is using loaded: Ardia's own tab budget doesn't put them to sleep and their profile isn't unloaded as idle for the next seconds (default 120, at most 300); on macOS Chromium's own discarding keeps them too, and elsewhere only while a debugger is attached. Each call replaces the session's held tabs; call again before the time ends to keep holding, and tabs.release ends it sooner. With untilDisconnect the hold has no timer and lasts until tabs.release from the same connection or until this connection closes, however the command ends (a crash or kill included), so it needs no renewing; it belongs to this connection, so another connection using the same session name can't replace or release it. With live, on macOS, held tabs keep drawing and laying out while in the background, so screenshots, hover and hit tests work without showing them; that ends with the hold

session.description: The holding session's own name; each session's holds are its own

tabs.description: Tab ids from windows or tabs.list; they replace what this session held

seconds.description: How long to hold them; ignored with untilDisconnect

untilDisconnect.description: Hold until this connection closes or tabs.release, with no timer to renew

live.description: Keep the held tabs drawing in the background (macOS)

result.name: tabs.consoleDelta
result.description: Console warnings and errors and uncaught page exceptions a tab logged since a watermark, from a ring of its last 200 that the engine keeps from the tab's creation. Pass the reply's next as after and its generation as generation on the following call; reset says the ring was replaced (the tab's page was swapped) and the read started over, dropped counts entries that left the ring before they were read, and withheld counts entries from frames DevTools may not inspect

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

after.description: The next of the previous reply; 0 or absent reads the whole ring

generation.description: The generation of the previous reply

result.result: {entries, generation, reset, next, last, dropped, withheld, errors, more}

result.name: tabs.diagnostics
result.description: A tab's console messages (every level, with uncaught exceptions and unhandled promise rejections marked by kind) and its network requests (method, address without its query, status, type, error and time taken), kept by the engine from the moment the tab was created, without DevTools attached. Entries share one sequence: pass the reply's nextSeq as since on the next call to get only what came after. dropped counts entries in that range the tab's fixed ring had already overwritten. Addresses lose their user name, password, query and fragment, and tokens, keys and passwords in messages read [redacted]. Private tabs keep none

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

since.description: Only entries with seq at or after this: the previous reply's nextSeq (default 0, everything kept)

onlyErrors.description: Only console warnings and errors and failed requests (a network error or a status of 400 or more)

limit.description: At most this many entries in all (default 200)

clear.description: Forget what this read covered, up to its nextSeq; cleared says whether it took

result.result: {tab, nextSeq, cleared?, console: [{seq, time, level, kind, message, source, line, frame, clipped?}], network: [{seq, time, method, url, status, type, frame, durationMs?, error?, failed, cached?}], dropped, more, capacity}

result.name: tabs.input
result.description: Real input to a tab's page, as the renderer gets it from the mouse and keyboard, so the page sees event.isTrusted true. It works on a tab in the background or off-screen without showing it, focusing its window or taking focus from another app, and attaches no debugger. x and y are CSS pixels from the page viewport's top left and must fall inside it; key takes a key value (a character, Enter, Tab, Backspace, Escape, ArrowLeft…) and code a key code (KeyA, Digit1…); text is inserted where the page's caret is, as typing or pasting does. Keys never reach Ardia's own shortcuts. acked says the renderer answered the last event within 2 s; text, which has no event to answer, says sent instead

result.name: devtools.attach
result.description: Open a DevTools session on a tab over this connection, with no approval prompt (the socket already checked who you are): every domain of that tab, its own iframes and workers through Target.setAutoAttach with flatten, and nothing else (no Target.getTargets, attachToTarget or createTarget; never a private tab or a chrome:// page). Events the tab sends arrive on this connection as devtools.event {session, method, params, sessionId?} (cut: true with bytes when one is over 900 KiB), and devtools.detached {session, reason} when it ends. It ends with devtools.detach, when the tab closes, when this connection closes or when control goes off. A tab that isn't on screen keeps drawing while the session is open

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

result.name: devtools.send
result.description: Send one DevTools command on a session from devtools.attach and answer its result. Target.setAutoAttach with flatten gives child sessions whose sessionId you pass here. sessionId.description: A child target's sessionId from Target.attachedToTarget, for flattened sessions

result.name: tabs.snapshot
result.description: The tab's page as a compact list of elements read from Chromium's accessibility tree across every frame (cross-site iframes and closed shadow roots included), each with a ref, role, accessible name, box in CSS pixels from the viewport's top left and a fingerprint of its role and name. When a modal dialog is open, only the topmost one is listed (scope: modal) unless wholePage. Interactive elements in view are hit-tested: one covered by something else says occludedBy with the covering element's ref. Refs stay the same for the same element; one whose element was replaced is found again by role and name when it's used

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

maxRefs.description: List at most this many elements (default 400)

maxTextBytes.description: Stop once names and values take this many bytes (default 65536)

interactiveOnly.description: List only elements you can act on

wholePage.description: List the whole page even when a modal dialog is open

occlusion.description: Hit-test elements in view to find covered ones (default true)

result.result: {tab, generation, viewport, scope, modal?, focused?, refs, truncated, counts, occlusion}

result.name: tabs.waitSettled
result.description: Wait until the tab's page has settled: no navigation in flight, the page done loading, no network request started since the wait began still running (requests longer than longRequestMs and event streams don't count) for quietMs, then the renderer's main thread idle and the next frame committed. Answers settled: false with waitingOn when timeoutMs passes; the wait ends early if the tab closes or this connection does

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

quietMs.description: How long the network must stay quiet (default 500)

longRequestMs.description: Requests running longer than this don't hold the wait (default 10000)

idle.description: Wait for the main thread to be idle (default true)

frame.description: Wait for the next frame to commit (default true)

result.result: {tab, settled, waitedMs, timedOut?, waitingOn?, navigations, network, idle, frame, loops, quietAtMs?, idleMs, frameMs}

result.name: tabs.hitTest
result.description: What a click at a ref's element, or at a point, would reach, across frames. When something else covers the element (a cookie banner, a dialog, an overlay), blocked is true and blocker names the covering layer with its box, and dismiss names the button inside it that most likely closes it (close, then reject, then accept), with up to 4 choices

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

x.description: A point in CSS pixels from the viewport's top left; give y too

y.description: The point's y in CSS pixels

result.result: {tab, point, verified, hit?, target?, rebound?, blocked, blocker?, dismiss?, choices?}

result.name: tabs.click
result.description: Click a ref's element, or a point, with trusted mouse input after the same hit test as tabs.hitTest: scrolls the element into view first, and when something covers it answers clicked: false with the blocker and the dismiss button instead of clicking it, unless force. It also refuses when the hit test can't confirm what the click reaches (reason: unverified) or when something moved over it after the pointer arrived (reason: moved)

tab.description: A tab id from windows or tabs.list

x.description: A point in CSS pixels from the viewport's top left; give y too

y.description: The point's y in CSS pixels

force.description: Click even when something covers the element

modifiers.description: Alt 1, Ctrl 2, Meta/Command 4, Shift 8, added together

result.result: {tab, clicked, point, verified, hit?, target?, rebound?, blocked, blocker?, dismiss?, choices?}

scale.description: Scale the image (default 1, the screen's pixels)
